examples.text: I have a very good appetite, have ate some excellent melons, and they have served me up some quails, the fattest and tenderest I have ever ate.
examples.ref: 1805, Maximilien de Béthune duc de Sully, Memoirs of Maximillian de Bethune, Duke of Sully, Prime Minister of Henry the Great […] , volume IV, page 171:

examples.text: As soon as all had ate, and the elder ones paid, the carriage was ordered; […]
examples.ref: 1813 January 27, [Jane Austen], chapter XVI, in Pride and Prejudice: […], volume II, London: […] [George Sidney] for T[homas] Egerton, […], →OCLC, page 192:

examples.text: The emotionless […] led the way into a large dining-room furnished with the severe simplicity of an apartment which is meant to be ate in, but never lived in; and at top of a table which would have accommodated eighteen persons Robert beheld Mr. Harcourt Talboys.
examples.ref: 1862, Mary Elizabeth Braddon, Lady Audley's Secret:

examples.text: “Haven't ate all the eggs, I hope? For I be hungry as a hunter[…]
examples.ref: 1929, Sir Arthur Thomas Quiller-Couch, Nicky-Nan, Reservist, page 27:

examples.text: So I'd have ate when me Dad had ate, sort of thing, I think, you know when he come home from work, I'd have waited for him, I wouldn't have said I wanted mine at four o'clock[…]
